correctness.rationale: Faber–Pandharipande Theorem 2 identifies the exact rational intersection coefficients. Two independent rational coefficient algorithms agree entrywise for g<=10. Every denominator and Minkowski prime power is calculated exactly. All subsets of the g+1 coefficients are exhausted and the genus-ten lower bound has a separate three-disjoint-prime-support argument; the cardinality-three set {0,1,3} meets all prime powers. No infinite-genus conclusion is asserted.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact minimum cardinality of a set of specified one-pointed linear Hodge denominators attaining the Minkowski least common multiple for genus 1 through 10, with the first obligatory three-witness genus and a three-prime-power disjoint-support obstruction. The primary source results give the aggregate lcm and all coefficients, but not this minimum-cardinality classification. Earlier Nørlund work remains a priority risk, explicitly disclosed.
residual_risks: The full Adelberg paper and other historical Nørlund congruence treatments were not inspected; the bounded witness counts may be implicit in coefficient congruences.
Finite-genus arithmetic is elementary given the known rational generating function; historical priority requires independent scholarly checking.

value.rationale: A motivated exact finite cutoff resolves how many natural one-pointed linear Hodge intersection numbers are required to witness the newly established universal Minkowski denominator. The first compulsory three-witness case has a structural three-prime-power obstruction, not just a numerical table. This answers a distinct denominator-complexity question for g<=10 without claiming a broad generalization.
